$comment: The defect the story names outright: an intent nothing on the menu serves, answered with a confident dispatch.
The CI workflow scaffolds a pipeline and no menu item runs a suite or repairs a failing test, so the user is
sent somewhere that cannot answer and is told nothing about it.
This is one of the two control cases, and its threshold is zero rather than a rate.
A frozen copy of one case of the live corpus and of the menu it is scored against. The pair (expected, menu)
is the whole input to scoreCase beside the reply, so both are stored here rather than read live: a replay has
to keep scoring the scenario it was derived against after the corpus moves on, and
npm run test:eval-routing-data already holds the live corpus against the shipped menu.

expected.rationale: No menu item executes a suite or repairs failing tests. CI scaffolds a pipeline and review judges tests; neither runs or fixes anything, and dispatching either sends the user somewhere that cannot answer.

derivation: The oracle expects decline and the action is route, so actionCorrect is false and confidentRouteOnUnservable is
true. routeCorrect is false as well, and for a second reason: it is only ever true on a case whose oracle
expects a route, and this one does not.
decidingTokens is [run, fix]. The reason carries neither, so tokensFound is 0.
declineOk is false because the action is not a decline. hedgedClearIntent is false: that control counts the
opposite mistake, and it is only ever counted on a case with one right answer.

answer.reason: your pipeline is red, so the continuous integration workflow is the place to start
